full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J:- The Rule issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the delay of 2091 days in filing the Civil Revisional application filed under section 5 of the Limitation Act before this Court should not be condoned and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner preferred the instant civil revision against the judgment dated  31.08.2005 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No.261 of 2005 affirming those of dated 16.05.2005 and 23.05.2005 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.96 of 2005 wherein the learned Senior Assistant Judge rejected the plaint of the plaintiff-petitioner. That in filing the revisional application there has been a delay of 2091 days and for condonation of the said delay the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner has preferred an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act contending inter alia that because of serious involvement of the petitioner with series of cases, she could not apply her mind towards filing of the revisional application against the impugned judgment and order of the court of appeal, which is unintentional latches of the petitioner for which the petitioner begs apology. The further case of the petitioner in a nutshell is such that after discussions with her lawyer the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner could understand that her grievances for removal of her from the post of Managing Director the only remedy is in civil suit and she ought to have filed a civil revision impugning the judgment and decree dated 31.08.2005 affirming the judgment and decree dated 16.05.2005. The petitioner is a foreigner as well as a woman and she fails to understand the legal status and implication of the impugned judgment and decree rather she felt that her remedy lies in company court in where her effort was ended without any result for her obtaining less than 10% shares and in this way there has been a delay of 2091 days. The plaintiff-appellant-petitioner apart from her aforesaid application for condonation of delay after filing an affidavit-in-reply against the affidavit-in-opposition of the defendant-respondent-opposite party No.2 contended that the Company Matter No.150 of 2005 ultimately dismissed on 08.05.2006. The certified copy of the judgment was received by the petitioner on 23.06.2008 and the petitioner preferred Leave to Appeal No.1697 of 2008 before the Hon'ble Appellate Division on 14.08.2008. The petitioner also filed before the Company Court the other Company Matter No.145 of 2008 on 09.08.2008 for rectification of the share register of the concerned Tea Hung Packaging (Bd.) Ltd. Thereafter, the petitioner instructed her lawyer not to press the case and accordingly it was dismissed on 29.07.2009 as being not pressed. The petitioner regrets for the delay caused for the aforesaid reason and prays for condonation of delay. 

 6. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate of the petitioner the learned counsels appearing on behalf of the opposite party controverted the submissions advanced from the side of the petitioner and submits that the grounds agitated from the side of the petitioner for condonation of the delay cannot be treated sufficient ground or reasonable excuse to condone the unusual delay of 2091 days. The learned Advocate further submits that the petitioner is not entitled to get any benefit under section 14 or section 5 of the Limitation Act inasmuch as due to willful negligence the petitioner did the mischief in not instituting the revisional application in proper forum within time. The learned Advocate also submits that the petitioner cannot claim to have committed any bonafide mistake on bonafide cause under section 14 of the Limitation Act as she was represented by her learned Advocates and she was all along negligent in committing the inordinate delay which cannot be categorized as bonafide mistake or delay whatsoever. The learned Advocate lastly submits that under the ambit of Limitation Act the petitioner is not entitled to have the relief as sought for as she was dormant in seeking her relief before appropriate forum within the stipulated time and as such the Rule is liable to be discharged. The learned Advocate in his concluding submissions referred some decisions of this Court and our Apex Court with regard to the ingredients of bonafide mistake or sufficient cause for condonation of delay. 

 9. Having gone through the relevant papers and the affidavit, supplementary affidavit, counter-affidavit-in-opposition and the papers annexed therewith I have the reason to inclined such a view that, applying section 5 of the Limitation Act the petitioner have prayed for condonation of 2091 days inordinate delay i.e. extension of limitation. The relevant law of limitation enjoins that the period of limitation can be enhanced in appropriate case only and where; the petitioner satisfies the court that he/she had sufficient cause for not preferring the case in time and in that case only the delay can be condoned. It is fact; that in the absence of any sufficient cause shown for condonation of delay of an inordinate delay which is 2091 days in preferring the civil revision the petitioner is not entitled to condonation of delay. If the petitioner can explain or can show satisfactory explanation for the delay; the delay can be ignored or condoned. Moreover; the delay can be condoned in the interest of justice in appropriate cases for substantive and plausible reasons if the petitioner is precluded to prefer the case within the prescribed period of limitations, but the negligent conduct, self-styled assumption of certain facts, ignorance of law or misapplication of law cannot form valid basis for condonation of delay. 

 10. In the instant case; I have come across that practically it is the case of the petitioner that due to wrong forum the delay occurred. In this context; the proposition of law is such; if a wrong forum have been chosen due to mistaken advice, generally the delay can be condoned but where the petitioner herself had stressed or chosen any forum which is ultimately wrong that very reason cannot be treated satisfactory explanation. Furthermore; the time consumed in pursuing case in wrong forum cannot be condoned under the ambit of section 5 of the Limitation Act. [Ref. Khajida Begum —vs.- Yasmeen, PLD 2001 (SC) 355]. 

 Apart from this; even absence of proper advice by a lawyer is not a ground for extension of time of limitation under section 05 or section 14 of Limitation Act. Where the mistake in approaching the wrong forum was committed by the counsel due to gross negligence and it did not appear on the face of the record that the counsel had shown due diligence and caution before moving the wrong forum, the only remedy for the client was to sue the counsel for damages for the loss suffered due to the negligence. [Ref. Bashir Ahmad—vs.- Md. Sharif, PLD 2001 (SC) 228]. 

 11. Consulting the decisions referred to above vis-à-vis; the respective case of the petitioner I have the reason to draw such inference that the conduct of the petitioner herself in choosing wrong forum cannot be treated 'sufficient cause' within the meaning of section 5 of the Limitation Act. Besides this; the ground of the application for condonation of delay as it appears is not proper to hold such a view that the mistake done by the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner was bonafide and she was diligent in filing the civil revision within time. Cause of delay as cited within the contents of the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act (IX of 1908) appears to be evasive and it is no doubt that only due to self-impression of the petitioner this delay of 2091 days occurred; which is not at all satisfactory. Moreover; it is settled that in the application filed under section 5 of the Limitation Act the petitioner is required to explain each day's delay to the satisfaction of the Court.
